summary: The stated thick-projection theorem is proved without error. Every predecessor is applied with its required convex-body, centroid, projection-radius, and positivity hypotheses; k>3/2 is exactly what makes the half-scale cut radius exceed 1/2. The sharp Grunbaum constant is substituted correctly, both bisection cases yield the corresponding component of L_m(k), the q_m(k)<=0 branch avoids reversing an inequality, and both threshold formulas are algebraically exact. The proof supports only the stated projection-thickness architecture and no unrestricted universal depth claim.
